newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Comercial del Plata gets Venezuela boost.
newsitem.headline: Comercial del Plata gets Venezuela boost.

text.p: A group led by Argentina's Compania General de Combustibles (CGC) won Friday a bid to operate a Venezuelan oil field, spelling good news for CGC's holding Comercial del Plata, analysts say.

"It is positive because Comercial needed those reserves," said Andres Pitchon, head of research of Merchant Bankers, an affiliate of Salomon Brothers. "They are investing in oil and gas, one of the higher upside areas of the conglomerate."
The consortium formed by CGC and Canada's Carmanah Resources Ltd bid $90.23 million for the contract to operate the Onado oil field in eastern Venezuela.

In a close bidding round between eight companies and consortiums, the Argentine-Canadian group narrowly beat out China National Petroleum Corp which bid $89.17 million and France's Total which offered $86.58 million.
"The close bidding suggests value for money," Pitchon said. "After such a win you can really be happy."
Andrea Sanguinetti, analyst for Consultatio Asset Management, said the Venezuelan deal spells is good both for CGC and its holding Comercial.
"The bid means CGC is not paying in excess, that they have done a good analysis of the area," she said.
"The deal increases CGC's relatively low oil and gas proven reserves, currently of 74,000 million barrels, equivalent to about six-years output."
It strenghthens earnings outlook for CGC and for Comercial, as CGC answered last year for about 40 percent of all Comercial's earnings, she added.
It is also good for Comercial, which plans to launch in July an IPO of an undetermined stake of CGC. "It will be selling a stake of a higher value company," said the analyst.
Pedro Sebess, managing director for Comercial, told Reuters the deal is very positive for the holding"
"It is a good boost, particularly when we are preparing to launch an IPO in the U.S. market," he said.
Comercial last week said it expected to raise about $330 million from the sale of stake in half a dozen local firms.
Sebess said Comercial expects to strongly reduce its debt to capital ratio to less than one to one, from 2/1 currently.
At March 31 Comercial's consolidated liabilities amounted to $931 million and net worth stood at $371 milion.
Cristina Hintz, portfolio manager of Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, said CGC's Venezuelan contract will help Comercial to improve its debt to capital ratio.
"Before the deal Comercial outlook was uncertain due to its debt level," she said. "Now it is in better position, and can improve results."
